note: Weekend + Monday-Asia sweep, every item source-verified (dates, numbers, attributions checked against the cited pages). Gathered ~11:00 SGT 20 Jul during the Asia session; published 17:45 SGT.

items.headline: Oil up ~30% from July lows flips Fed odds toward a September HIKE; silver pinned near 8-month lows
items.summary: TradingEconomics reports markets now price roughly a 53% probability of a Fed rate hike in September, up from 47% a day earlier, as the oil surge (~30% above July lows) rekindles inflation fears; Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack added hawkish warnings. Silver bounced 1.67% to $56.84 Monday morning but remains near its lowest levels in eight months, with Iran declaring the ceasefire effectively collapsed and saying it intercepted four vessels in Hormuz over the weekend.
items.actionable: This is the single most important development for your top risk: rising hike expectations are overpowering the war bid in silver and gold — consider whether to trim or hedge the levered silver position into Monday's bounce rather than averaging down.

items.headline: Silver bounces 1.7% to $56.84 in Monday Asia trade, but holds near 8-month lows as Fed-hike odds climb
items.summary: Silver rose above $56/oz on Monday, last at $56.84 (+1.67% on the day), recovering from Friday's rout but still pinned near its lowest levels in eight months. The bounce is happening against a hostile backdrop: oil's ~30% surge from July lows on the US-Iran conflict has markets pricing a 53% chance of a September Fed rate HIKE (up from 47% a day earlier), with multiple Fed officials sounding hawkish — a direct headwind for non-yielding metals.
items.actionable: The intraday bounce relieves pressure on the levered silver position today, but the driver of the selloff (rate-hike repricing) is intact and strengthening. Treat $55.6-56 as the level to watch — a hawkish surprise into the Jul 28-29 FOMC could break it. Consider whether leverage sizing survives another 5-10% leg down.

items.headline: US troop deaths appear to cross Trump's red line; Iran MOU collapses, oil jumps ~3%
items.summary: Two US soldiers were killed and one is missing after an Iranian attack on a base in Jordan, with a third killed in Iraq disposing of a downed Iranian drone — deaths Fortune says would appear to cross Trump's stated red line for ending the earlier ceasefire, and the memorandum of understanding signed last month has collapsed. Sunday-evening futures were mixed (Dow -61 pts / -0.12%, S&P -0.05%, Nasdaq +0.08%) while WTI rose 2.75% to $84.76 and Brent 3.2% to $90.92. Notably, gold fell 0.53% to $3,997 despite the escalation, and ship-tracking data shows no vessels have transited the US-backed Hormuz corridor.
items.actionable: Expect a firm oil bid supporting your energy sleeve Monday/Tuesday, but do not count on gold or silver to hedge the war risk — metals are trading off rates, not geopolitics, so keep risk tight on the levered silver position.

items.headline: Iranian attacks inflict severe damage on Kuwait oil facility; US strikes hit night 8, blockade tightens
items.summary: Kuwait Petroleum Corporation reported 'severe material losses' at a vital oil-sector facility from repeated Iranian attacks (reported July 18) — the war's supply damage is now spreading beyond Iran and shipping to Gulf producer infrastructure. Per July 19 updates, US forces ran an eighth consecutive night of strikes (coastal surveillance, air defense, maritime and missile/drone storage targets) and, enforcing the naval blockade, have redirected five commercial vessels and disabled one; the US toll since the war began stands at 16 killed and over 430 wounded.
items.actionable: Attacks on GCC oil infrastructure widen the supply-risk premium beyond Hormuz transit — supportive of your WTI/energy exposure, but negative for bonds and for rate-sensitive S-REITs if crude keeps climbing.

items.headline: Beijing steps in: state funds buy, CSRC convenes; Hang Seng +2%, Tencent +2.5%, Alibaba +4.1%
items.summary: Hong Kong stocks rallied Monday as Beijing moved to shore up markets: the CSRC invited market participants to a Monday meeting on promoting stable and healthy market development (RTHK), and two major state-backed funds disclosed fresh equity purchases in a coordinated display of support (Bloomberg/Seeking Alpha, 20 Jul). The Hang Seng opened up 272 points (1.11%) at 24,835 and extended to +484 points (1.97%) at 25,046 mid-morning, with the Tech Index up 2.2% at 4,724 and the China Enterprises Index up 1.43% at 8,252. Individual movers at the open (Dim Sum Daily): Tencent +2.5%, Alibaba +4.1%, Kuaishou +4.1%, Meituan +2.6%, Xiaomi +2%; AI supply-chain names Montage +8.7% and SMIC +4.5% — China chips trading on domestic AI demand, decoupled from Friday’s US SOX rout.
items.actionable: Direct tailwind for your Tencent/HK-China tech book — the 'national team' put is back under the market, making China tech one of the few risk pockets with explicit policy support this week.

items.headline: PBoC holds Loan Prime Rates at 3.00% (1-yr) and 3.50% (5-yr) at July fixing
items.summary: At this morning's monthly fixing, the People's Bank of China left its benchmark Loan Prime Rates unchanged — the one-year LPR at 3.00% and the five-year at 3.50%. The hold comes despite Q2 GDP slowing to 4.3% year-on-year, its weakest pace since Q4 2022, leaving markets to look elsewhere (fiscal policy, the late-July Politburo meeting) for fresh stimulus signals.
items.actionable: No fresh easing tailwind for your China/HK exposure today — the market rallied anyway, so the burden shifts to fiscal delivery. Next catalyst is the late-July Politburo meeting; don't count on PBoC rate cuts to drive Tencent from here.

items.headline: Late-July Politburo meeting expected to ease tone; RMB6.8tn unused bond quota is the real ammunition
items.summary: A pre-weekend preview of the Politburo meeting (typically held the final week of July) expects Beijing to acknowledge growth pressure after the weaker Q2, call for stronger counter-cyclical adjustment and accelerate already-announced measures — but not launch a major new stimulus package. Key figure: around RMB6.8 trillion of this year's approved government bond issuance quota remained unused at end-June, so fiscal implementation, not rhetoric, is the durable signal. Property support to ease gradually (looser city-level restrictions, inventory programs) aimed at stabilisation, not another boom; PBoC rate/RRR cuts unlikely unless growth deteriorates further.
items.actionable: The Politburo meeting is THIS WEEK's biggest scheduled catalyst for your Tencent/HK-tech and broader China exposure. Today's LPR hold makes fiscal follow-through the swing factor — watch for concrete bond-issuance acceleration, not just softer language, before sizing up China risk.

items.headline: Gold flat at $4,016 Monday, hovering near nine-month lows around the $4,000 line
items.summary: Gold traded at $4,015.76/oz (-0.03%) in Monday Asia hours, drifting toward $4,000 and close to nine-month lows. Commentary cites the same driver as silver: escalating US-Iran attacks pushing oil higher, stoking inflation fears and lifting September Fed hike odds to ~53% from 47%, with Cleveland Fed's Beth Hammack joining hawkish colleagues. Geopolitical safe-haven demand is being overwhelmed by rate-hike repricing.
items.actionable: $4,000 is the psychological floor for the gold and gold-miner sleeve. Gold failing to catch a bid during an active shooting war is a warning sign — the rates channel is dominating. Miners (leveraged to spot) remain exposed if $4,000 gives way.

items.headline: Oil spikes above $85 then retreats to $81.80 as US-Iran diplomatic feelers emerge; Kuwait oil facility hit over weekend
items.summary: WTI briefly topped $85/bbl in early Monday trade before paring to around $81.80 (-0.84%) after Iran's Foreign Ministry signaled negotiations with the US could continue if they serve the country's national interests. Weekend escalation was real: attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz and an Iranian strike on an oil facility in Kuwait on Saturday, per Kuwait Petroleum Corp. A significant geopolitical premium remains embedded in crude (Brent $87.72).
items.actionable: Near-term negative for the oil/energy sleeve (pullback from $85), but genuine de-escalation would be the single best macro catalyst for the rest of the portfolio — it would deflate the Fed-hike repricing crushing silver, gold, semis and HK tech. Watch Iran mediation headlines through Monday-Tuesday; they matter more than any single position.

items.headline: STI seen extending losses Monday after back-to-back declines below 5,510
items.summary: RTTNews' Sunday-night preview (published 19 July, 8:03pm ET) notes the Singapore market has fallen in consecutive sessions, slumping more than 50 points or 0.9% cumulatively, leaving the Straits Times Index just beneath the 5,510-point plateau — off its record ~5,561. It flags the index 'may take further damage on Monday' on tech weakness, elevated oil prices and Middle East concerns.
items.actionable: Your STI/Singapore-bank sleeve is pulling back from records rather than breaking down — a ~1% drift on war and tech jitters, not a bank-specific problem. With Q2 bank earnings due early August, this looks like consolidation; no action needed unless 5,400 area gives way.

items.headline: Three S-REITs — Keppel DC REIT, Suntec, Mapletree Industrial — report Thursday 23 July
items.summary: The Smart Investor's Monday preview flags all three reporting on 23 July. Keppel DC REIT comes in strongest: last DPU S$0.02833 (+13.2% YoY), distributable income +20.7% YoY to S$74.6m, leverage 35.1% with ~S$550m debt headroom, and rental reversion of roughly 51% on renewed contracts. Suntec REIT's last DPU was S$0.01936 (+23.9% YoY) though NPI edged up just 0.3%; guidance is ~5% Singapore office and ~10% retail rental reversion. Mapletree Industrial Trust is the laggard: full-year DPU S$0.1271 (-6.3% YoY), gross revenue -7.9%, NPI -8.6%, leverage 34% rising to ~37.5% after its May 2026 perpetual redemption.
items.actionable: First real test of your S-REIT sleeve this earnings season is Thursday. Keppel DC's data-centre momentum (51% rental reversions) is the bull case; MIT's shrinking DPU is the warning. Check which of the three you actually hold before Thursday and expect dispersion, not a sector-wide move.

items.headline: Semiconductor rout deepens: AMD -5%, Nvidia -3%; $3.3T in global chip value erased since June 22
items.summary: On Friday 17 July AMD fell 5% to $477.81, Intel 4% to $93.24 and Nvidia 3% to $201.60, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) down 3% to $515.76 in early trading. Global semiconductor stocks have shed $3.3 trillion in market value since June 22, nearing bear-market territory. Two triggers: Chinese startup Moonshot's release of Kimi K3, a downloadable open-weight model challenging the more-compute-is-necessary premise, and TSMC guiding to higher-than-anticipated capital expenditures at its Q2 report, stoking margin-compression fears across the supply chain. AMD's ~163x P/E was flagged as especially vulnerable if AI spending expectations reset.
items.actionable: Direct hit on the portfolio's US semiconductor sleeve. The selloff is narrative-driven (cheap Chinese open-weight models + TSMC capex) rather than demand-driven — TSMC's own revenue guide remains a record. Watch whether Monday's Asia session extends the rout into TSMC Taipei/ADR and HK tech before assuming the -11% month in SOX is done.

items.headline: Bitcoin ETFs log 4th straight day of inflows ($132.3M on Jul 17, IBIT-led); BTC steady at $64,695 in Monday Asia hours
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $132.3M net on Thursday Jul 17 — a fourth consecutive positive day — led by BlackRock's IBIT with $136.5M (FBTC saw a $4.2M outflow). BTC was ~$64,018 at the time of reporting. As of 11:22am SGT Monday (Jul 20), BTC trades at $64,694.96 (+0.04% over 24h) and ETH at $1,875.00 (+0.48%) — crypto rode out the weekend war headlines sideways-to-up, holding the $64k shelf.
items.actionable: A persistent institutional ETF bid under $64k while metals and semis get sold makes BTC the portfolio's relative-strength holder. No action needed; the $62,450 area flagged as support last week is the invalidation level if war/Fed news worsens.

items.headline: MP Materials hits 52-week low of $44.33, down 28% over the past year, as China export-control listing weighs
items.summary: MP Materials touched a 52-week low of $44.33 on 17 July, down 28.09% over the past 12 months, cutting market cap to $8.09 billion. The slide comes despite a Q1 beat (EPS $0.03 vs -$0.01 expected; revenue $90.65M vs $73.57M projected) and reflects the overhang from China's Ministry of Commerce adding MP Materials to its export control list. Sell-side remains constructive: BofA Securities holds a Buy with an $85 target and DA Davidson a Buy at $82 — implying ~85% upside from the low.
items.actionable: The portfolio's rare-earth policy thesis (DoD partnership, US onshoring) is intact but price action is fighting it — the China entity-list designation is doing real damage. A close in the low $40s despite $82-85 analyst targets signals the market is pricing escalation risk; watch for any US counter-measures on critical minerals as the next catalyst either way.

items.headline: Malaysia parliamentary committee probes Lynas's $96M Pentagon rare-earths supply deal
items.summary: A Malaysian parliamentary special select committee on international relations and trade, chaired by MP Wong Chen, met on 16 July to examine Lynas Rare Earths' $96 million four-year supply agreement with the US Department of Defense. The probe — triggered by complaints from over 20 civil society groups including Greenpeace Malaysia that the contract supports US military operations backing Israel in Gaza — will feed a government position to be issued within two weeks. Lynas runs the world's largest rare-earths processing plant in Malaysia and is the only major producer of separated rare earths outside China, making Malaysian regulatory goodwill critical.
items.actionable: Political-risk overhang on the portfolio's Lynas position: the Kuantan plant is the company's core asset and Malaysia has form on restricting Lynas's operating licence. Two dated catalysts to watch: the Malaysian government's official position (due within two weeks, i.e. by ~end July) and Lynas's June-quarter results and webcast on 22 July.
